text:
lee: Noticing a sudden pile-up of tiny and medium pods Pending in eu-west1 (mostly eu-west1b). Scheduler logs show a flood of topologyHint misses and a bunch of nodes flapping Ready->NotReady for kube-proxy conntrack pressure.

sam: any infra deploys?

lee: nothing in cluster-manager. But yesterday we decreased conntrack defaults in a kube-proxy rollout (PR #4990) to make room for high-cardinality services. suspect it's too low for our gpu-serving fanout.

avni: that explains the iptables errors I was seeing. heatmap from last hour: 80% of small pods landed on 3 racks (rack-7/8/9) and other racks are underutilized. topology-aware hints are making scheduler prefer certain AZ-local nodes when conntrack signals noisy routes.

kevin: can you paste the kube-proxy logs?

lee: pasted snippet:
```
Mar 18 10:12:03 kube-proxy[1234]: E03018 10:12:03 conntrack.go:218] failed to ensure conntrack is functional: could not allocate table: conntrack: failed to allocate buckets
Mar 18 10:12:07 kube-proxy[1234]: W03018 10:12:07 proxysync.go:512] Service endpoints change triggered heavy programming, skipping some local endpoints
```

olga: we've seen this pattern before. conntrack exhaustion -> kube-proxy starts failing endpoint sync -> scheduler observation of unstable nodes de-prioritizes them -> packing concentrates on a few "stable" racks -> frag + preempt churn when those racks eventually hit thermal/egress limits.

sam: customer impact?

avni: hosted customers in eu-west1 have ~4% increase in cold-start latency for model-inference and we burned ~1.2k GPU-minutes in the last 2 hours due to repeated restarts.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3287 (eu-west1 conntrack exhaustion -> scheduling skew). Severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3287

kevin: mitigation plan proposals: 
- quick rollback of kube-proxy conntrack limit to previous value (fast).
- temporarily disable topologyAwareHints or lower topology affinity weight for "workload-size=small" so scheduler spreads small pods.
- taint the three magnet racks (7/8/9) no-new-tiny for 15m while autoscaler smooths.

olga: agree but watch large-gang placement. don't break 8x GPU co-locates. If we lower topology hints, enable an exception that preserves gangAffinity label for big jobs.

lee: I'll open an infra-roll PR to revert conntrack to 262144 and patch kube-proxy helm chart with a short TTL.

sam: can we also bump kubelet evictionGracePeriod so pods don't restart immediately into the same broken nodes?

kevin: yes, set evictionGracePeriod=120s for the affected nodes via node-annotations during mitigation.

avni: I'll prepare a scheduler-policy canary to lower rackAffinityScore from 100->30 for label workload-size=small and apply to eu-west1 only. We'll watch gang-placement test.

lee: issuing taints on racks 7/8/9 now and cordon non-critical tiny pools.

oncall-bot: @oncall-eng notified: Lee triggered incident INC-2026-3287.

olga: followup: we should add conntrack headroom to our GPU pool autoscaler docs and include a preflight test for kube-proxy conntrack settings in the release pipeline. this is a repeatable frag pattern.

sam: noted. after rollback I'll run a short synthetic workload that exercises 5000 simultaneous client sockets to verify headroom.

kevin: estimate: rollback + taint + policy canary should stabilize in ~25-30m. cost/impact: expect to avoid another ~2k GPU-minutes if stabilized.

lee: thanks all. checklist: revert kube-proxy conntrack (lee), taint/cordon racks 7/8/9 (lee), schedule policy canary (avni), bump evictionGracePeriod (kevin), run synthetic socket test (sam). reconvene in 30 if not stable. :thumbsup:
